topic: Large Language Models for Automated Code Review: Techniques, Benchmarks, and Industrial Deployment

per_sentence.text: Pioneering work in this area, such as CodeReviewer, introduced pre-training objectives specifically designed for code review activities, demonstrating that task-aware pre-training significantly outperforms general-purpose models (Li et al., 2022).

judge.rationale: The abstract explicitly states that CodeReviewer uses four pre-training tasks tailored for code review and outperforms previous state-of-the-art pre-training approaches, directly supporting the claim of task-aware pre-training significantly outperforming general-purpose models.

per_sentence.text: Similarly, sequence editing models like CoditT5 have been proposed to handle the inherent structure of code diffs, treating code changes as edits rather than generation from scratch (Li et al., 2022).

judge.rationale: The cited paper proposes CodeReviewer, a general pre-trained model for code review tasks, but does not mention CoditT5 or the specific approach of treating code changes as edits rather than generation from scratch.

per_sentence.text: Furthermore, benchmarks for code generation, such as HumanEval, have been adapted to evaluate the code refinement capabilities of LLMs (Chen et al., 2021).

judge.rationale: The cited paper introduces HumanEval for measuring functional correctness of code generation from docstrings but does not mention adapting it to evaluate code refinement capabilities of LLMs.

per_sentence.text: The development of context-rich, repository-level benchmarks is essential for accurately gauging the efficacy of LLMs in realistic code review settings (Hou et al., 2023).

judge.rationale: The cited paper is a broad systematic literature review on LLMs for software engineering and does not specifically discuss or argue for the necessity of context-rich, repository-level benchmarks for code review evaluation.

per_sentence.text: The rise of open-source models tailored for code, such as Code Llama, has facilitated on-premise deployments, allowing companies to fine-tune models on their internal codebases while retaining complete control over their intellectual property (Roziere et al., 2023).

judge.rationale: The evidence confirms Code Llama is an open model for code released under a permissive license, which enables on-premise deployment and fine-tuning, but it does not explicitly state that this allows companies to retain complete control over their intellectual property.

per_sentence.text: Effective integration also involves seamlessly embedding the LLM into existing developer tools and IDEs, ensuring that the AI acts as a collaborative assistant rather than a disruptive barrier (Fan et al., 2023).

judge.rationale: The cited abstract discusses LLMs for software engineering broadly and mentions hybrid techniques but does not address embedding LLMs into developer tools or IDEs as a collaborative assistant.

per_sentence.text: The quality of the training data also poses a challenge; models trained on open-source code may learn suboptimal practices or reinforce existing biases present in the data (Zhang et al., 2023).

judge.rationale: The cited evidence examines student perceptions and intentions regarding generative AI use in education, but it does not address training data quality, open-source code, or the learning of suboptimal practices and biases.
